```{python}
import html
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from IPython.display import HTML, display

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd().parent))
from edwait.data import registry, short_name
facilities = registry()
context_path = Path("comparisons.json")
context = json.loads(context_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if context_path.exists() else None
```

```{python}
from dashboard.overview import build_overview
from plotly.offline import get_plotlyjs

if context is None or not any(entry["history"] for entry in context["facilities"]):
    display(HTML("<p class='empty-chart'>All-hospital history is unavailable until comparison preparation succeeds.</p>"))
else:
    overview = build_overview(context, facilities)
    # Quarto moves library output into the document head. Keep the plot in a
    # separate output so its container stays here, immediately above the legend.
    display(HTML("<script>" + get_plotlyjs() + "</script>"))
    display(HTML(overview.to_html(full_html=False, include_plotlyjs=False,
                                div_id="all-hospitals-plot", default_height="100%",
                                post_script="document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('overview-ready'));",
                                config={"responsive": True, "displayModeBar": False})))
    from edwait.data import LOCAL_TIMEZONE, timestamp
    from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
    prepared = timestamp(context["generated_at"]).astimezone(ZoneInfo(LOCAL_TIMEZONE))
```


Overview: toggle hospital names to show or hide lines; double-click or Shift-click
to isolate one. Both charts follow the time control above. The overview rescales
to the visible lines in that window and updates with each site build. Current
readings refresh separately, about every minute. Times are America/Chicago.
Collection gaps over 20 minutes stay blank.

Usual range: the middle 50% of a hospital's readings across the preceding 28 local
days, excluding the observation's entire day. The median and historical percentile
describe published readings, not patient outcomes or care quality. Percentiles
count lower readings plus half of tied readings. Zero is preserved; its upstream
meaning is unconfirmed.

We compare the same weekday/weekend group and neighboring hours (±1 hour), then
fall back to ±2 hours, then all days if needed. A reference needs eight adequately
covered days, 64 readings, and 75% of expected 15-minute slots. A contributing day
also needs 75% coverage. Support and fallbacks appear with the selected hospital.

Above/below usual: the outer 10% of the reference distribution plus at least a
10-minute difference from its median. Recent direction: the latest reading minus
the median of at least two readings 40–80 minutes earlier, with changes under
10 minutes labeled little change. This describes recent movement, not a forecast.
Current comparisons pause on unconfirmed freshness, failed reference fetches,
references two hours old, or the next local midnight.

These 20 configured Baptist facilities are not a complete regional directory.
Collection time does not establish the provider's update time. Serious conditions
receive priority through [triage](https://www.baptistonline.org/services/emergency).

Historical coverage spans the loaded reference window and is measured against
observed batches; baseline slot coverage also counts missing calendar dates.
Request latency describes HTTP collection, not patient waits or hospital capacity.

```{python}
if context is None:
    display(HTML("<p>No valid historical observations are available until comparison preparation succeeds.</p>"))
else:
    display(HTML("<p>Historical artifact prepared: " + html.escape(context["generated_at"]) + "</p>"))
    display(HTML("<pre>" + html.escape(json.dumps(context["coverage"], indent=2)) + "</pre>"))
    names = {f["slug"]: f["display_name"] for f in facilities}
    rows = "".join("<tr><th scope='row'>" + html.escape(names.get(r["slug"], r["slug"])) +
                   "</th><td>" + str(r["samples"]) + "</td><td>" + str(r["median_ms"]) +
                   "</td><td>" + str(r["p95_ms"]) + "</td></tr>" for r in context["latency"])
    display(HTML("<div class='table-scroll'><table><caption>Request latency · seven days</caption>"
                 "<thead><tr><th scope='col'>Facility</th><th scope='col'>Requests</th><th scope='col'>Median (ms)</th>"
                 "<th scope='col'>95th percentile (ms)</th></tr></thead><tbody>" + rows + "</tbody></table></div>"))
```
